Fold the row keys into one row-heading column

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_stub.Rd

plan_stub() makes the stub: the row keys (the block of each analysis variable, the category under it) folded into one indented column with a heading row per block, as stub_cols() does. It belongs to the display half of the pipe, after the cells and rows are declared and before the header and pages. By default the fold happens inside as_rtftables(), after grouping and pagination have read the keys.

Usage

plan_stub(
  .plan,
  vars = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  indent = NULL,
  group_summary = NULL,
  before = FALSE
)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

vars

The row keys to fold, as stub_cols(vars = ). Left out, they are worked out from the plan: the names of table_plan(rows = ) and its label column, without a grouping carrier. With one column (a table of one row heading), that column is the stub, renamed name, and nothing is folded.

name

The name of the folded column, stub_cols(label = ), and so its header text unless plan_col_header() says otherwise: "Characteristic". Not the same as table_plan(label = ), the column whose values are the row text.

indent

The non-breaking spaces per nesting level, stub_cols(indent = ) (default 4). plan_row_group(mode = "indent") reads the indent this writes.

group_summary

Which leaf values mark a row as its group's summary, folding its statistics onto the group's heading row, as stub_cols(group_summary = ): "empty", "parent", "all" or "none".

before

FALSE (default) folds the stub inside as_rtftables(), after grouping and pagination have had their say. TRUE folds it first, with stub_cols(), which is what a condition of plan_cell_style() needs: only then can it see the rows that will be printed. The two do not always give the same table: folded first, the row keys are gone before a page split or a row group could read them, so plan_paginate_group(col = ) naming one of them no longer finds it.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; stub_cols().

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 3),
  variable  = rep(c("AGE", "SEX", "SEX"), 2),
  .label    = rep(c(NA, "F", "M"), 2),
  .kind     = rep(c("continuous", "categorical", "categorical"), 2),
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "n", "n"), 2),
  stat      = c(61.2, 12, 8, 63.5, 9, 11))
p <- table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c(Mean = "{mean:.1f}"), categorical = "{n}") |>
  plan_labels(AGE = "Age (years)", SEX = "Sex")

# Minimal: one stub column with a heading row per variable
plan_apply(p |> plan_stub(name = "Characteristic"), "pages")[[1]]
#> ───────────────────────────────
#> Characteristic  Placebo  Active
#> ───────────────────────────────
#> Age (years)                    
#>     Mean         61.2     63.5 
#> Sex                            
#>     F             12       9   
#>     M              8       11  
#> 
#> <rtftable> 5 rows x 3 columns
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#> 

# A narrower indent, folded first so that a condition can read the
# printed rows: the heading rows (no indent) in bold
pages <- p |>
  plan_stub(name = "Characteristic", indent = 2, before = TRUE) |>
  plan_cell_style(cols = "Characteristic",
                  bold = ~ !grepl("^ ", Characteristic)) |>
  plan_apply("pages")
pages[[1]]
#> ───────────────────────────────
#> Characteristic  Placebo  Active
#> ───────────────────────────────
#> Age (years)                    
#>   Mean           61.2     63.5 
#> Sex                            
#>   F               12       9   
#>   M                8       11  
#> 
#> <rtftable> 5 rows x 3 columns
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#>   Cell styles: set (5 rows)
#>
